newsitem.title: CHILE: Blue whale dies after washing up on Chilean beach.
newsitem.headline: Blue whale dies after washing up on Chilean beach.

text.p: A whale believed to be a blue whale, the largest and rarest species in the world, was washed up on a southern Chilean beach but died a few hours after being found, local officials said on Friday.
"Unfortunately the whale was very battered and died this morning (Friday)," regional Gov. Rabindranath Quinteros told La Segunda newspaper.

The whale, which measured 79 feet (24 meters) and weighed 40 tonnes, was found on a beach on Thursday by villagers from the fishing community of Llico Bajo, 600 miles (1,000 km) south of Santiago. Descriptions suggested it was a blue whale but it still has to be confirmed by experts, Quinteros said.

There have been few sightings off the Chilean coast of this species of whale, which is more commonly found in the northern hemisphere. Blue whales have been declared in danger of extinction after hunting nearly wiped them out earlier this century.
